# MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Master Services Agreement (this "**Agreement**") is entered into as of March 1, 2024 (the "**Effective Date**") by and between **Keisaiv Therapeutics, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 410 Halvorsen Parkway, Suite 900, Princeton, New Jersey 08540 ("**Client**"), and **Kedoul Specialty Logistics, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company with its principal place of business at 2275 Corridor Way, Building C, Memphis, Tennessee 38118 ("**Provider**"). Client and Provider are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

**RECITALS**

A. Client is a specialty pharmaceutical company that commercializes Velnorix injection, a refrigerated biologic product, in the United States.

B. Provider operates temperature-controlled warehousing and distribution facilities and provides third-party logistics, specialty distribution and patient support hub services to pharmaceutical manufacturers.

C. Client wishes to engage Provider, and Provider wishes to be engaged, to perform such services on the terms of this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants set out below, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

Capitalized terms used in this Agreement have the meanings set out below or elsewhere in this Agreement.

1.1 "**Affiliate**" means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting securities of, or the power to direct the management of, such entity.

1.2 "**Applicable Law**" means all federal, state and local laws, regulations, guidance and orders applicable to a Party or the Services, including the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the Drug Supply Chain Security Act, state wholesale distribution licensing laws, the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 and its implementing regulations ("**HIPAA**"), and federal and state anti-kickback and privacy laws.

1.3 "**Business Day**" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or day on which national banks in New York, New York are authorized or required to close.

1.4 "**Confidential Information**" has the meaning given in Section 10.1.

1.5 "**Covered Products**" means any pharmaceutical product commercialized by Client or its Affiliates, now or in the future, including Velnorix.

1.6 "**Data Processing Addendum**" or "**DPA**" means the Data Processing Addendum between the Parties dated as of the Effective Date governing Provider's processing of Personal Data in connection with the Services, as amended from time to time.

1.7 "**Fees**" means the fees for the Services set out in the applicable Statement of Work.

1.8 "**Hub Services**" means the patient support hub services described in a Statement of Work, which may include benefits verification, prior authorization support, co-pay program administration, patient intake and case management, and coordination of shipments to patients and sites of care.

1.9 "**Personal Data**" means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person, including protected health information as defined under HIPAA, that Provider receives, creates or processes in connection with the Services.

1.10 "**Quality Agreement**" means the GDP Quality Agreement between the Parties governing the storage, handling and distribution of Velnorix, as amended from time to time.

1.11 "**Service Level Schedule**" means the Service Level Schedule attached to or executed under this Agreement setting out the service levels, measurement methods and service credits applicable to the Services.

1.12 "**Services**" means the third-party logistics, warehousing, order-to-cash, specialty distribution and Hub Services described in this Agreement and in each Statement of Work, together with any related services reasonably necessary for their performance.

1.13 "**Statement of Work**" or "**SOW**" means a written statement of work executed by both Parties that references this Agreement and describes Services to be performed and the applicable Fees.

1.14 "**Temperature Excursion**" means any deviation, of any duration, outside the 2°C to 8°C labeled storage range.

1.15 "**Territory**" means throughout the world.

1.16 "**Velnorix**" means Client's Velnorix (injection) product, in all strengths and presentations, as approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

## 2. APPOINTMENT AND SERVICES

2.1 **Services.** Provider shall perform the Services described in each Statement of Work in accordance with this Agreement, the Quality Agreement, the DPA, the Service Level Schedule and Applicable Law. The initial Statement of Work, executed concurrently with this Agreement, covers warehousing, distribution and Hub Services for Velnorix.

2.2 **Statements of Work.** Each Statement of Work is governed by and incorporated into this Agreement. Either Party may propose additional Statements of Work, and no Statement of Work is binding unless signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. A Statement of Work may be amended only by a written change order signed by both Parties.

2.3 **Related Agreements.** Concurrently with this Agreement, the Parties have entered into the Quality Agreement and the DPA. The Service Level Schedule forms part of this Agreement.

2.4 **Exclusivity.** During the Term, Client appoints Provider as Client's exclusive provider of third-party logistics, specialty distribution and patient support hub services for the Covered Products in the Territory, and Client shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, engage any third party to perform services that are the same as or substantially similar to the Services for any Covered Product in the Territory. Client shall cause its Affiliates to comply with this Section 2.4 as if they were parties to this Agreement.

2.5 **Facilities.** Provider shall perform the

Services at the facilities identified in the applicable Statement of Work. Provider shall not relocate the storage of Velnorix to a different facility without Client's prior written consent and completion of any qualification activities required under the Quality Agreement.

2.6 **Licenses and Registrations.** Provider shall obtain and maintain, at its own expense, all licenses, registrations and permits required under Applicable Law to perform the Services, including state wholesale distributor and third-party logistics provider licenses, and shall provide copies to Client on request.

## 3. SERVICE LEVELS

3.1 **Performance Standards.** Provider shall perform the Services in accordance with the service levels set out in the Service Level Schedule.

3.2 **Service Credits.** If Provider fails to meet a service level, Provider shall issue the service credits set out in the Service Level Schedule, subject to the limits stated in that schedule. Service credits are a price adjustment reflecting the reduced value of the Services and are not Client's exclusive remedy for a material breach of this Agreement.

3.3 **Reporting and Reviews.** Provider shall deliver monthly performance reports in the form required by the Service Level Schedule. The Parties' relationship managers shall meet at least quarterly to review performance, open corrective actions and forecasts.

## 4. FEES AND PAYMENT

4.1 **Fees.** Client shall pay the Fees set out in each Statement of Work. Fees exclude applicable sales, use and similar taxes, which Client shall pay other than taxes on Provider's net income.

4.2 **Invoicing.** Provider shall invoice Client monthly in arrears. Each invoice shall itemize Fees by Statement of Work and shall reflect any service credits accrued in the preceding month.

4.3 **Payment.** Client shall pay undisputed amounts within forty-five (45) days after receipt of a correct invoice. Client may withhold amounts disputed in good faith by written notice describing the dispute, and the Parties shall work to resolve the dispute within thirty (30) days.

4.4 **Fee Adjustments.** Provider may adjust the Fees once per contract year, effective on an anniversary of the Effective Date, by written notice delivered at least ninety (90) days in advance. No adjustment shall exceed the lesser of three percent (3%) and the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers for the preceding twelve (12) months.

4.5 **Audit.** Provider shall keep complete and accurate records supporting its invoices for at least three (3) years after the relevant invoice date. Client may audit those records once per calendar year on thirty (30) days' notice.

## 5. CLIENT OBLIGATIONS

5.1 **Forecasts.** Client shall provide Provider with a rolling twelve (12) month non-binding forecast of inbound shipments and expected order volumes, updated monthly.

5.2 **Product Information.** Client shall provide Provider with the labeling, storage requirements, shipping specifications and other product information reasonably required to perform the Services, and shall notify Provider promptly of any change.

5.3 **Program Rules.** For Hub Services, Client shall provide written program rules, eligibility criteria and approved patient communications. Provider shall not deviate from approved program rules or communications without Client's written approval.

## 6. PROVIDER OBLIGATIONS

6.1 **Standard of Performance.** Provider shall perform the Services in a professional and workmanlike manner, consistent with good distribution practices and the standards of care generally observed by leading specialty pharmaceutical logistics providers in the United States.

6.2 **Compliance.** Provider shall comply with Applicable Law, the Quality Agreement and Client's written policies provided to Provider in advance. Provider shall not offer or pay any remuneration to any health care provider, patient or payer in connection with the Services other than as expressly directed by Client under an approved patient support program.

6.3 **Serialization and Traceability.** Provider shall maintain transaction information, transaction history and transaction statements for Velnorix as required by the Drug Supply Chain Security Act and shall respond to verification requests within the time required by Applicable Law.

6.4 **Adverse Events and Complaints.** Provider shall forward to Client any adverse event, product complaint or medical information request it receives regarding Velnorix within one (1) Business Day of receipt, in the manner set out in the applicable Statement of Work.

6.5 **Debarment.** Provider represents that neither it nor any person performing Services is debarred, excluded or suspended under 21 U.S.C. § 335a or from any federal health care program, and shall notify Client immediately if this representation ceases to be true.

## 7. PERSONNEL AND SUBCONTRACTORS

7.1 **Personnel.** Provider shall assign qualified and appropriately trained personnel to perform the Services and may replace them on reasonable notice. Provider shall designate a relationship manager as Client's primary point of contact.

7.2 **Subcontractors.** Provider shall not subcontract any portion of the Services involving the storage or physical handling of Velnorix or the processing of Personal Data without Client's prior written consent. Provider remains fully responsible for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors.

## 8. DATA PROTECTION

8.1 **DPA.** Provider shall process Personal Data only in accordance with the DPA, Client's documented instructions and Applicable Law. To the extent required by HIPAA, the DPA operates as a business associate agreement between the Parties.

8.2 **Security Incidents.** Provider shall notify Client of any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, use or disclosure of, Personal Data in accordance with the timelines and procedures set out in the DPA.

## 9. TITLE, RISK OF LOSS AND PRODUC

9.1 **Title.** Title to Velnorix and all other Client inventory remains with Client at all times. Provider shall keep Client inventory free of liens and encumbrances arising through Provider and shall not hold itself out as the owner of any Client inventory.

9.2 **Custody.** Velnorix is in Provider's custody from the time Provider accepts delivery at its facility until delivery to the consignee designated in the applicable order, including while in transit with any carrier engaged by Provider.

9.3 **Product Loss.** Provider shall bear the replacement cost of any Velnorix that is lost, stolen, damaged, or subject to a Temperature Excursion while in Provider's custody, except to the extent such loss results from Client's negligence or a defect in Velnorix existing at the time Provider accepted delivery. Replacement cost means Client's fully burdened cost of goods for the affected units plus reasonable costs of investigation, quarantine and destruction. Provider shall pay or credit such amounts within thirty (30) days after Client's written demand.

9.4 **Notification and Quarantine.** Provider shall notify Client of any loss, damage or Temperature Excursion affecting Velnorix and shall quarantine affected units in accordance with the Quality Agreement pending Client's disposition decision.

9.5 **Inventory Counts.** Provider shall conduct cycle counts in accordance with the applicable Statement of Work and a full physical inventory at least once per calendar year, and shall reconcile any variance with Client within ten (10) Business Days.

## 10. CONFIDENTIALITY

10.1 **Definition.** "Confidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of a Party in connection with this Agreement that is marked confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential, including pricing, forecasts, patient program rules and business plans. Confidential Information does not include information that (a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the receiving Party; (b) was lawfully known to the receiving Party without restriction before disclosure; (c) is lawfully obtained from a third party without restriction; or (d) is independently developed without use of the disclosing Party's Confidential Information.

10.2 **Obligations.** Each Party shall protect the other's Confidential Information with at least reasonable care, use it only to perform or receive the Services, and disclose it only to its employees, Affiliates, subcontractors and advisors who need to know it and are bound by obligations at least as protective as this Section 10.

10.3 **Compelled Disclosure.** A Party may disclose Confidential Information as required by law or court order, provided it gives the disclosing Party prompt notice where legally permitted and cooperates in seeking protective treatment.

10.4 **Duration.** The obligations in this Section 10 continue for five (5) years after expiration or termination of this Agreement, and indefinitely for trade secrets. Personal Data is governed by the DPA.

## 11. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

11.1 **Pre-existing Materials.** Each Party retains ownership of its pre-existing materials, systems and know-how.

11.2 **Client Materials and Deliverables.** All reports, patient program materials, data compilations and other deliverables prepared specifically for Client under a Statement of Work become the property of Client upon payment in full. Provider grants Client a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use any Provider pre-existing materials incorporated into such deliverables to the extent necessary to use the deliverables.

11.3 **Trademarks.** Provider shall not use Client's names, trademarks or logos without Client's prior written consent, except as required to perform the Services.

## 12. TERM AND TERMINATION

12.1 **Initial Term.** This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for 36 months from the Effective Date (the "**Initial Term**"), unless earlier terminated in accordance with this Section 12.

12.2 **Renewal.** Upon expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive three (3) year renewal terms (each, a "**Renewal Term**" and, together with the Initial Term, the "**Term**"), unless either Party delivers written notice of non-renewal to the other Party no earlier than two hundred ten (210) days and no later than one hundred eighty (180) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Initial Term or Renewal Term. A notice of non-renewal delivered at any other time shall be of no force or effect.

12.3 **Termination for Cause.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work by written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure the breach within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice describing it.

12.4 **Termination for Insolvency.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately by written notice if the other Party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or becomes the subject of any bankruptcy, receivership or similar proceeding that is not dismissed within sixty (60) days.

12.5 **Regulatory Termination.** Client may terminate this Agreement immediately by written notice if Provider loses any license required to perform the Services, receives a warning letter or equivalent regulatory action relating to its handling of pharmaceutical products, or breaches Section 6.5.

12.6 **Transition Assistance.** Upon expiration or termination for any reason, Provider shall, for up to one hundred eighty (180) days at Client's request and at the rates then in effect, continue to perform the Services and cooperate in the orderly transfer of Client inventory, records and patient cases to Client or its designee.

12.7 **Effect of Termination.** Upon expiration or termination, Client shall pay all undisputed Fees for Services performed through the effective date, and Pr

ovider shall return all Client inventory and Confidential Information and handle Personal Data as required by the DPA. Sections 4.5, 9, 10, 11, 12.6, 12.7, 13, 14 and 16 survive expiration or termination.

## 13. INDEMNIFICATION

13.1 **By Provider.** Provider shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Client, its Affiliates and their officers, directors and employees from and against all third-party claims, losses, damages, penalties and reasonable attorneys' fees arising out of (a) Provider's breach of this Agreement, the Quality Agreement or the DPA; (b) Provider's negligence or willful misconduct; (c) Provider's violation of Applicable Law; or (d) any unauthorized use or disclosure of Personal Data in Provider's possession or control.

13.2 **By Client.** Client shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Provider and its officers, directors and employees from and against all third-party claims, losses, damages and reasonable attorneys' fees arising out of (a) product liability claims relating to Velnorix, except to the extent caused by Provider's handling of Velnorix; (b) Client's negligence or willful misconduct; or (c) Client's violation of Applicable Law.

13.3 **Procedure.** The indemnified Party shall give prompt written notice of any claim, allow the indemnifying Party to control the defense and settlement (provided no settlement imposes any obligation or admission on the indemnified Party without its consent), and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense.

## 14. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

14.1 **Exclusion of Consequential Damages.** Except for liability under Sections 9.3, 10 and 13, or arising from a Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, neither Party is liable for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, or for lost profits, arising out of this Agreement.

14.2 **Cap.** Except for liability under Sections 9.3, 10 and 13, or arising from a Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, each Party's aggregate liability arising out of this Agreement shall not exceed the total Fees paid and payable under this Agreement in the twenty-four (24) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

## 15. INSURANCE

15.1 Provider shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the Term and for two (2) years thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of at least $5,000,000 per occurrence; (b) warehouse legal liability and cargo insurance covering the full replacement value of Client inventory in Provider's custody; (c) professional and technology errors and omissions insurance of at least $5,000,000 per claim; (d) cyber liability insurance of at least $10,000,000 per claim; and (e) workers' compensation insurance as required by law. Provider shall name Client as an additional insured where customary and deliver certificates of insurance on request.

## 16. GENERAL

16.1 **Governing Law.** This Agreement is governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

16.2 **Forum.** Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state or federal courts located in New York County, New York for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

16.3 **Notices.** Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with confirmation by courier, to the addresses stated on the signature page or such other address as a Party designates by notice. Notices are effective on receipt.

16.4 **Order of Precedence.** In the event of any conflict among this Agreement and the related documents, the Quality Agreement shall govern with respect to quality, storage and handling matters; the DPA shall govern with respect to Personal Data; and otherwise this Agreement shall govern, followed by the Service Level Schedule, followed by the Statements of Work.

16.5 **Assignment.** Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, except that either Party may assign this Agreement without consent to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or substantially all of the business to which this Agreement relates, on written notice to the other Party.

16.6 **Independent Contractors.** The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship.

16.7 **Force Majeure.** Neither Party is liable for delay or failure in performance caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided it gives prompt notice and uses commercially reasonable efforts to resume performance. Force majeure does not excuse Provider's obligations to maintain temperature-controlled storage, backup power and business continuity measures required by the Quality Agreement.

16.8 **Amendment and Waiver.** This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both Parties. No waiver is effective unless in writing, and no failure or delay in exercising a right operates as a waiver.

16.9 **Severability.** If any provision of this Agreement is held unenforceable, it shall be enforced to the maximum extent permissible and the remaining provisions shall remain in effect.

16.10 **Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument.

**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the Parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

# DATA PROCESSING ADDENDUM

This Data Processing Addendum (this "**DPA**") is entered into as of March 1, 2024 (the "**Effective Date**") by and between **Keisaiv Therapeutics, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation ("**Client**"), and **Kedoul Specialty Logistics, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Provider**"). Client and Provider are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**." This DPA supplements the Master Services Agreement between the Parties dated as of the Effective Date (the "**Agreement**").

**RECITALS**

A. Under the Agreement, Provider performs third-party logistics, specialty distribution and Hub Services for Velnorix. In doing so, Provider receives, creates and processes Personal Data, including protected health information of patients enrolled in Client's patient support program.

B. The Parties wish to set out the terms on which Provider processes Personal Data. Where HIPAA requires it, these terms also serve as a business associate agreement under 45 C.F.R. §§ 164.502(e) and 164.504(e).

The Parties therefore agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 Capitalized terms used but not defined in this DPA have the meanings given in the Agreement, including "Affiliate," "Applicable Law," "Business Day," "Hub Services," "Personal Data," "Services," "Statement of Work" and "Velnorix."

1.2 "**Data Protection Laws**" means all Applicable Law relating to the privacy, security or processing of Personal Data. This includes HIPAA, the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act and their implementing regulations, the Federal Trade Commission Act, and state laws on health data privacy, consumer privacy, data security and breach notification.

1.3 "**HIPAA**" has the meaning given in Section 1.2 of the Agreement.

1.4 "**PHI**" means protected health information as defined in 45 C.F.R. § 160.103, limited to information that Provider creates, receives, maintains or transmits on behalf of Client or Client's patient support program.

1.5 "**Processing**" means any operation performed on Personal Data, whether or not by automated means. This includes collection, recording, organization, storage, adaptation, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure, transmission, alignment, restriction, erasure and destruction. "**Process**" and "**Processed**" have corresponding meanings.

1.6 "**Security Incident**" means any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, use, disclosure, modification or destruction of, Personal Data. It also means any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized interference with the systems used to Process Personal Data. It includes any "breach of unsecured protected health information" as defined in 45 C.F.R. § 164.402.

1.7 "**Subprocessor**" means any third party engaged by Provider to Process Personal Data on Provider's behalf.

## 2. SCOPE AND ROLES

2.1 **Scope.** This DPA applies to all Personal Data Processed by Provider, its Affiliates or its Subprocessors in connection with the Services. This includes patient intake, benefits verification, prior authorization support, co-pay program administration, case management and coordination of shipments to patients and sites of care.

2.2 **Roles.** For the Personal Data, Client is the party that determines the purposes and means of Processing. Provider Processes Personal Data solely on Client's behalf. To the extent Client or Client's patient support program acts as or on behalf of a covered entity or business associate under HIPAA, Provider acts as Client's business associate or subcontractor business associate.

2.3 **Details of Processing.** The categories of data subjects, categories of Personal Data, and nature and purpose of the Processing are described in Annex A.

## 3. PROVIDER OBLIGATIONS

3.1 **Instructions.** Provider shall Process Personal Data only:
(a) to perform the Services;
(b) in accordance with the Agreement, this DPA and Client's other documented instructions; and
(c) as required by Data Protection Laws.

Provider shall promptly notify Client if, in Provider's reasonable opinion, an instruction violates Data Protection Laws.

3.2 **Restrictions.** Provider shall not:
(a) sell, rent or license Personal Data;
(b) share Personal Data for cross-context behavioral advertising;
(c) use Personal Data for Provider's own commercial purposes;
(d) combine Personal Data with data from other sources, except as necessary to perform the Services; or
(e) de-identify Personal Data for any purpose not authorized in writing by Client.

3.3 **Minimum Necessary.** Provider shall limit its use and disclosure of PHI, and its requests for PHI, to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose, in accordance with 45 C.F.R. § 164.502(b).

3.4 **Confidentiality of Personnel.** Provider shall ensure that every person authorized to Process Personal Data:
(a) is bound by written confidentiality obligations;
(b) receives privacy and security training at least annually; and
(c) has access only to the Personal Data required for that person's role.

3.5 **Permitted Disclosures.** Provider may disclose PHI only:
(a) to Client;
(b) to patients, health care providers, pharmacies, payers and other persons as required to perform the Hub Services under Client's approved program rules; or
(c) as required by law, subject to Section 10.3 of the Agreement.

## 4. SECURITY

4.1 **Safeguards.** Provider shall implement and maintain administrative, physical and technical safeguards that:
(a) comply with the HIPAA Security Rule, 45 C.F.R. Part 164, Subpart C; and
(b) are appropriate to the risk presented by the Processing.

The minimum required measures are described in Annex B.

4.2 **Encryption.** Provider shall encrypt Personal Data in transit and at rest. Encryption shall use industry-standard algorithms consistent with guidance issued by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

4.3 **Risk Assessment.** Provi

keisaiv_kedoul_data_processing_addendum.md, page 2 of 3:
der shall perform a documented security risk analysis at least annually and after any material change to the systems used to Process Personal Data. Provider shall remediate identified risks in a timely manner.

4.4 **Certification.** Provider shall maintain a SOC 2 Type II report, or an equivalent independent assessment, covering the systems used to Process Personal Data. Provider shall deliver the current report to Client on request.

## 5. SECURITY INCIDENTS

5.1 **Notification.** Provider shall notify Client in writing of any Security Incident without undue delay, and in any event within forty-eight (48) hours after Provider discovers it. The notice shall include, to the extent then known:
(a) the nature of the Security Incident;
(b) the categories and approximate number of individuals and records affected;
(c) the identity of each affected individual;
(d) the likely consequences; and
(e) the measures taken or proposed to contain and remediate it.

Provider shall supplement the notice as further information becomes available.

5.2 **Investigation and Remediation.** Provider shall promptly:
(a) investigate the Security Incident;
(b) take all reasonable steps to contain, mitigate and remediate it; and
(c) preserve all relevant logs and evidence.

Provider shall cooperate with Client and any forensic examiner Client engages.

5.3 **Notifications to Third Parties.** Client shall determine whether and how to notify affected individuals, regulators, the media or other third parties. Provider shall not make any such notification without Client's prior written approval, except where Data Protection Laws require it.

5.4 **Costs.** Provider shall reimburse Client's reasonable costs for any Security Incident arising from a breach of this DPA by Provider or its Subprocessors. These costs include:
(a) forensic investigation;
(b) notification to individuals and regulators;
(c) call center support;
(d) credit or identity monitoring for affected individuals for at least twenty-four (24) months; and
(e) any other remediation required by Data Protection Laws.

5.5 **Unsuccessful Attempts.** This Section 5 is satisfied as to unsuccessful attempts if Provider reports them in aggregate on Client's request. Unsuccessful attempts include pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to Personal Data.

## 6. SUBPROCESSORS

6.1 **Consent.** Consistent with Section 7.2 of the Agreement, Provider shall not engage any Subprocessor without Client's prior written consent. Annex C lists the Subprocessors approved as of the Effective Date.

6.2 **Subprocessor Terms.** Provider shall enter into a written agreement with each Subprocessor before the Subprocessor Processes any Personal Data. That agreement shall impose data protection obligations no less protective than this DPA. Where PHI is involved, it shall include a subcontractor business associate agreement that complies with 45 C.F.R. § 164.504(e).

6.3 **Responsibility.** Provider remains fully responsible to Client for the acts and omissions of each Subprocessor.

## 7. INDIVIDUAL RIGHTS AND ASSISTANCE

7.1 **Individual Requests.** Provider shall forward to Client, within five (5) Business Days of receipt, any request from an individual to exercise rights under Data Protection Laws. These include rights of access, amendment, accounting of disclosures, deletion or opt-out. Provider shall not respond to the request except as Client directs.

7.2 **HIPAA Rights.** Provider shall:
(a) make PHI available for access and amendment as required by 45 C.F.R. §§ 164.524 and 164.526; and
(b) document disclosures and provide the information required for an accounting of disclosures under 45 C.F.R. § 164.528.

In each case, Provider shall act within the time reasonably required for Client to meet its obligations.

7.3 **Assistance.** Provider shall provide reasonable assistance to Client with:
(a) privacy impact assessments;
(b) responses to regulatory inquiries; and
(c) compliance with Data Protection Laws relating to the Services.

7.4 **Books and Records.** Provider shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to the use and disclosure of PHI available to the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. This obligation applies for purposes of determining compliance with HIPAA.

## 8. DATA LOCATION AND TRANSFERS

8.1 **Location.** Provider shall store and Process Personal Data only within the United States. Provider shall not permit remote access to Personal Data from outside the United States without Client's prior written consent.

## 9. AUDIT

9.1 **Audit Rights.** Client may audit Provider's compliance with this DPA, either itself or through an independent auditor bound by confidentiality obligations. Audits may take place once per calendar year on thirty (30) days' written notice. Client may also audit at any time after a Security Incident or on a regulator's request.

9.2 **Remediation.** Provider shall promptly remediate any non-compliance identified in an audit. Provider shall report the remediation to Client in writing.

## 10. RETURN AND DELETION

10.1 **On Termination.** Upon expiration or termination of the Agreement, and after completion of any transition assistance under Section 12.6 of the Agreement, Provider shall, at Client's election:
(a) return all Personal Data to Client or Client's designee in a mutually agreed format; or
(b) securely destroy all Personal Data.

Provider shall certify the return or destruction in writing within thirty (30) days.

10.2 **Retention Required by Law.** If Applicable Law requires Provider to retain any Personal Data, the following applies:
(a) Provider shall extend the protections of this DPA to that Personal Data;
(b) Provider shall limit further use and disclosure to the purposes that make return or destruction infeasible; and
(c) Provider shall destroy the Personal Data when the retention requirement ends.

## 11. TERM; LIABILITY

11.1 **Term.*

**Data subjects:** The following persons, as they relate to Velnorix:

- Benefits verification and prior authorization records.
- Co-pay program enrollment and financial eligibility data.

- Adverse event and product complaint information.

4. Vulnerability scanning at least monthly, and independent penetration testing at least annually.
5. Endpoint protection, patch management and secure configuration standards.
6. Documented incident response, business continuity and disaster recovery plans, tested at least annually.

# GDP QUALITY AGREEMENT

This GDP Quality Agreement (this "**Quality Agreement**") is entered into as of March 1, 2024 (the "**Effective Date**") by and between **Keisaiv Therapeutics, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation ("**Client**"), and **Kedoul Specialty Logistics, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Provider**"). Client and Provider are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**." This Quality Agreement is entered into under the Master Services Agreement between the Parties dated as of the Effective Date (the "**Agreement**").

**RECITALS**

A. Client holds the approved Biologics License Application for Velnorix and is responsible for the quality of Velnorix placed on the market.

B. Under the Agreement, Provider stores, handles and distributes Velnorix on Client's behalf. Provider also coordinates shipments of Velnorix to patients and sites of care as part of the Hub Services.

C. This Quality Agreement allocates the Parties' quality responsibilities for those activities in accordance with good distribution practices and Applicable Law.

The Parties therefore agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Quality Agreement have the meanings given in the Agreement, including "Affiliate," "Applicable Law," "Business Day," "Hub Services," "Services," "Statement of Work" and "Velnorix."

1.1 "**Applicable GDP Requirements**" means all Applicable Law and regulatory guidance governing the storage, handling and distribution of prescription drugs and biologics in the United States. This includes 21 C.F.R. Parts 203 and 205, the Drug Supply Chain Security Act, United States Pharmacopeia General Chapters <1079> and <659>, and state wholesale distribution and third-party logistics provider requirements.

1.2 "**CAPA**" means a corrective and preventive action.

1.3 "**Change**" means any proposed change to a Facility, to equipment or systems used to store, monitor or ship Velnorix, to shipping configurations or lanes, or to any procedure governing activities under this Quality Agreement.

1.4 "**Deviation**" means any departure from this Quality Agreement, an approved procedure or an Applicable GDP Requirement.

1.5 "**Facility**" means each Provider facility at which Velnorix is received, stored or shipped, as identified in the applicable Statement of Work and qualified under Section 4.

1.6 "**Lot**" means a specific quantity of Velnorix identified by a unique lot number assigned by Client or its manufacturer.

1.7 "**Product Complaint**" means any written, electronic or oral communication alleging a deficiency in the identity, quality, durability, reliability, safety, effectiveness or performance of Velnorix, including its packaging and labeling.

1.8 "**Quarantine**" means the physical and system segregation of Velnorix, with status controls, so that it cannot be shipped pending a disposition decision by Client.

1.9 "**Temperature Excursion**" means any deviation outside the 2°C to 8°C labeled storage range lasting more than sixty (60) consecutive minutes, as recorded by a qualified temperature monitoring device.

1.10 "**Quality Unit**" means, for each Party, the function responsible for quality assurance under this Quality Agreement, as identified in Annex 1.

## 2. SCOPE AND RESPONSIBILITIES

2.1 **Scope.** This Quality Agreement applies to Velnorix injection, distributed solely in the United States. It covers receipt, storage, inventory control, order picking, packing, shipping, returns handling and the related records maintained by Provider under the Agreement.

2.2 **Client Responsibilities.** Client is responsible for:
(a) release of each Lot for distribution;
(b) all disposition decisions for Velnorix in Quarantine, including decisions following a Temperature Excursion;
(c) stability data and product-specific storage and shipping specifications;
(d) recalls, market withdrawals and regulatory reporting to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration; and
(e) approval of shipping configurations and packaging qualification protocols.

2.3 **Provider Responsibilities.** Provider is responsible for:
(a) storing and handling Velnorix in accordance with its labeling, Client's specifications and Applicable GDP Requirements;
(b) maintaining qualified Facilities, equipment and shipping systems;
(c) maintaining a quality management system adequate for the Services;
(d) identifying, documenting and investigating Deviations within its control; and
(e) cooperating with Client in recalls, investigations and regulatory inspections.

2.4 **Responsibility Matrix.** Annex 2 sets out a summary allocation of responsibilities. Annex 2 is a summary only and is to be read with the body of this Quality Agreement.

## 3. QUALITY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM

3.1 **Quality System.** Provider shall maintain a documented quality management system covering document control, training, Change control, Deviation management, CAPA, internal audits, supplier and carrier qualification, and management review.

3.2 **Procedures.** Provider shall maintain written standard operating procedures for all activities under this Quality Agreement. On request, Provider shall provide Client with copies of procedures that apply specifically to Velnorix.

3.3 **Training.** Provider shall train all personnel who handle Velnorix or its records on the applicable procedures before they perform those tasks, and at least annually after that. Provider shall keep training records.

3.4 **Internal Audits.** Provider shall perform internal quality audits of each Facility at least annually.

## 4. FACILITIES AND EQUIPMENT

4.1 **Qualification.** Before storing Velnorix at a Facility, Provider shall complete installation, operational and performance qualification of the refrigerated storage areas. This includes a temperature mapping study under both summer and winter conditions. Provider shall provide the qualification reports to Client for review.

4.2 **Requalification.** Provider shall repeat temperature

keisaiv_kedoul_quality_agreement.md, page 2 of 3:
mapping at least every three (3) years and after any Change that could affect temperature distribution.

4.3 **Monitoring Equipment.** Provider shall continuously monitor storage temperatures using calibrated sensors with alarm capability, traceable to national standards. Provider shall calibrate each sensor at least annually.

4.4 **Alarms.** Provider shall configure alarms to alert responsible personnel at all times, including outside business hours. Provider shall test alarm functionality at least quarterly.

4.5 **Backup Power and Continuity.** Each Facility shall have automatic backup power sufficient to maintain refrigerated storage for at least seventy-two (72) hours. Provider shall maintain a written business continuity plan for Velnorix storage and shipping, including contingency storage at a qualified alternate location. Provider shall test the plan at least annually.

4.6 **Pest Control, Security and Sanitation.** Provider shall maintain documented programs for pest control, cleaning and physical security of each Facility, with access to Velnorix storage areas restricted to authorized personnel.

## 5. STORAGE AND HANDLING

5.1 **Storage Conditions.** Provider shall store Velnorix refrigerated at 2°C to 8°C, protected from light in its original carton, and shall not freeze it.

5.2 **Receipt.** On receipt of each inbound shipment, Provider shall:
(a) verify the shipment against Client's advance shipping notice;
(b) review in-transit temperature data before placing Velnorix into available inventory;
(c) inspect for visible damage; and
(d) verify product identifiers as required by the Drug Supply Chain Security Act.

Velnorix shall remain in Quarantine until receipt is complete and Client has released the Lot.

5.3 **Inventory Control.** Provider shall manage inventory on a first-expired, first-out basis unless Client directs otherwise. Provider shall not ship any unit with less than the remaining shelf life specified by Client in the applicable Statement of Work.

5.4 **Temperature Records.** Provider shall keep continuous temperature records for each storage area and each shipment and shall make them available to Client on request.

5.5 **Temperature Excursions.** Provider shall notify Client's Quality Unit of any Temperature Excursion affecting Velnorix within one (1) Business Day after discovery. Provider shall promptly place all affected units in Quarantine and shall provide Client with the temperature data, the duration and the minimum and maximum temperatures recorded. Affected units shall remain in Quarantine until Client makes its disposition decision.

5.6 **Damaged and Suspect Product.** Provider shall place in Quarantine any Velnorix that is damaged, suspected of being counterfeit or illegitimate, or otherwise unfit for distribution. Provider shall notify Client within one (1) Business Day.

## 6. SHIPPING AND TRANSPORTATION

6.1 **Shipping Configurations.** Provider shall ship Velnorix only in shipping configurations qualified for the applicable lane and season and approved by Client.

6.2 **Carriers.** Provider shall use only carriers qualified under its supplier qualification procedure and approved by Client. Provider remains responsible for Velnorix while in transit with carriers it engages.

6.3 **In-Transit Monitoring.** Each shipment of Velnorix shall include a calibrated temperature indicator or data logger as specified by Client. Provider shall instruct consignees on how to report indicator alarms.

6.4 **Licensing of Consignees.** Provider shall verify, before each shipment, that each consignee is appropriately licensed or authorized under Applicable Law to receive Velnorix.

## 7. RETURNS, RECALLS AND COMPLAINTS

7.1 **Returns.** Provider shall receive returned Velnorix only as authorized by Client and shall place all returns in Quarantine. Returned Velnorix shall not be returned to saleable inventory without Client's written disposition.

7.2 **Recalls.** Client shall direct all recalls and market withdrawals. Within the timeframes Client specifies, Provider shall:
(a) provide distribution records identifying consignees by Lot;
(b) place remaining inventory of affected Lots in Quarantine; and
(c) support consignee notification and reconciliation of returned units.

Provider shall participate in a mock recall at least annually at Client's request.

7.3 **Product Complaints.** Provider shall forward Product Complaints to Client within one (1) Business Day of receipt, consistent with Section 6.4 of the Agreement. Provider shall investigate any Product Complaint relating to its own activities and report its findings to Client.

## 8. DEVIATIONS, CAPA AND CHANGE CONTROL

8.1 **Deviations.** Provider shall document and investigate each Deviation. Provider shall notify Client within one (1) Business Day of any Deviation that may affect the quality of Velnorix. Investigations shall be completed within thirty (30) days unless Client agrees to an extension, and shall identify root cause and proposed CAPA.

8.2 **CAPA.** Provider shall implement CAPA within agreed timelines and verify its effectiveness. Provider shall report the status of open CAPA in the quarterly reviews held under Section 3.3 of the Agreement.

8.3 **Change Control.** Provider shall notify Client in writing at least sixty (60) days before implementing any Change that may affect Velnorix. Provider shall not implement the Change without Client's written approval. Emergency Changes required to protect Velnorix may be implemented immediately, with notice to Client within one (1) Business Day.

## 9. RECORDS

9.1 **Record Keeping.** Provider shall keep complete and accurate records of all activities under this Quality Agreement. This includes receipt, storage, temperature monitoring, shipping, returns, Deviations, CAPA, training and qualification records.

9.2 **Retention.** Provider shall retain records for at least the longer of:
(a) six (6) years after creation; and
(b) one (1) year after expiry of

keisaiv_kedoul_quality_agreement.md, page 3 of 3:
 the relevant Lot.

Provider shall not destroy records without first offering them to Client.

9.3 **Electronic Records.** Electronic systems used to create or maintain quality records shall be validated and shall maintain secure, time-stamped audit trails consistent with 21 C.F.R. Part 11, to the extent applicable.

## 10. AUDITS AND INSPECTIONS

10.1 **Client Audits.** Client may audit each Facility and Provider's quality records once per calendar year on thirty (30) days' notice. Client may also audit at any time for cause, including after a significant Deviation or Temperature Excursion.

10.2 **Regulatory Inspections.** Provider shall notify Client within one (1) Business Day of any regulatory inspection or inquiry relating to Velnorix or to Facilities where Velnorix is stored. Provider shall provide copies of any resulting observations and its responses. Client may review those responses before submission, to the extent they relate to Velnorix.

## 11. TERM AND AMENDMENT

11.1 **Term.** This Quality Agreement remains in effect for the Term of the Agreement and for so long after that as Provider holds any Velnorix or quality records relating to Velnorix.

11.2 **Review.** The Quality Units shall review this Quality Agreement at least every two (2) years and on any material Change in the Services.

11.3 **Amendment.** This Quality Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by the Quality Unit heads of both Parties. Annex 1 may be updated by written notice from either Party for its own contacts.

**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the Parties have executed this Quality Agreement as of the Effective Date.

# SERVICE LEVEL SCHEDULE

This Service Level Schedule (this "**Schedule**") is entered into as of March 1, 2024 (the "**Effective Date**") by and between **Keisaiv Therapeutics, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation ("**Client**"), and **Kedoul Specialty Logistics, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Provider**"). It forms part of the Master Services Agreement between the Parties dated as of the Effective Date (the "**Agreement**").

## 1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

1.1 **Purpose.** This Schedule sets out:
(a) the service levels that apply to the Services;
(b) how the service levels are measured and reported; and
(c) the service credits that apply under Section 3.2 of the Agreement.

1.2 **Scope.** This Schedule applies to the Services performed for Velnorix under the initial Statement of Work. It covers:
(a) outbound shipments from the Facilities to consignees located in the fifty states of the United States and the District of Columbia (the "**U.S. Lanes**"); and
(b) the Hub Services provided to patients and health care providers located in the United States.

1.3 **Definitions.** Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Schedule have the meanings given in the Agreement or, where applicable, in the Quality Agreement.

## 2. DEFINITIONS

2.1 "**Conforming Order**" means an order for Velnorix that meets all of the following conditions:
(a) Provider receives it through the agreed order channel by the Order Cut-Off Time on a Business Day;
(b) it contains complete ship-to, consignee license and product information;
(c) it is for released inventory available at the Facility; and
(d) it is not on credit, compliance or regulatory hold at Client's direction.

2.2 "**Order Cut-Off Time**" means 3:00 p.m. Central Time, or another time specified in the applicable Statement of Work.

2.3 "**Measurement Period**" means each calendar month.

2.4 "**Monthly Fees**" means the total Fees invoiced under the applicable Statement of Work for Services performed in the relevant Measurement Period. Pass-through freight, packaging and other reimbursable costs are excluded.

2.5 "**Service Level Failure**" means Provider's failure to achieve a Service Level in a Measurement Period.

2.6 "**Service Level**" means each performance standard set out in Section 3.

## 3. SERVICE LEVELS

3.1 **Order Fulfillment.** Provider shall ship 98% of Conforming Orders on the same Business Day. Measurement: the number of Conforming Orders shipped on the Business Day of receipt, divided by the total number of Conforming Orders received in the Measurement Period.

3.2 **Order Accuracy.** Provider shall ship at least 99.8% of order lines with no errors. An order line is in error if it has the wrong product, strength, presentation, quantity, Lot, consignee or shipping configuration. Measurement: the number of error-free order lines shipped, divided by the total number of order lines shipped in the Measurement Period, as confirmed by consignee discrepancy reports and Provider's investigation.

3.3 **On-Time Delivery.** At least 98.5% of shipments on the U.S. Lanes shall be delivered by the delivery date committed for the applicable service level selected for the order. Measurement: carrier proof-of-delivery data. Shipments delayed by events described in Section 6.1 are excluded.

3.4 **Shipping Configuration Compliance.** 100% of shipments of Velnorix shall be made in a qualified shipping configuration approved by Client for the applicable lane and season, as required by Section 6.1 of the Quality Agreement. Each shipment shall include the temperature indicator or data logger required by Section 6.3 of the Quality Agreement.

3.5 **Temperature Excursion Notification.** For 100% of Temperature Excursions affecting Velnorix in Provider's custody, Provider shall notify Client's Quality Unit and place the affected units in Quarantine. Notification shall be given within one (1) Business Day after discovery, in accordance with Section 5.5 of the Quality Agreement.

3.6 **Inventory Accuracy.** Provider shall maintain inventory record accuracy of at least 99.9% by unit, by Lot, as measured by cycle counts and by the annual physical inventory under Section 9.5 of the Agreement.

3.7 **Benefits Verification Turnaround.** Provider shall complete at least 95% of benefits verifications within two (2) Business Days after receipt of a complete patient enrollment form.

3.8 **Hub Call Answer Rate.** Provider shall answer at least 90% of inbound calls to the patient support program line within thirty (30) seconds. The call abandonment rate shall not exceed 5%. This Service Level applies during the hub operating hours specified in the applicable Statement of Work.

3.9 **Adverse Event and Complaint Forwarding.** Provider shall forward to Client 100% of adverse events, Product Complaints and medical information requests regarding Velnorix within one (1) Business Day of receipt, in accordance with Section 6.4 of the Agreement.

## 4. MEASUREMENT AND REPORTING

4.1 **Data.** Provider shall measure each Service Level using its warehouse management, transportation, temperature monitoring and hub case management systems. Provider shall keep the underlying data for at least three (3) years, consistent with Section 4.5 of the Agreement, and shall make it available to Client on request.

4.2 **Monthly Report.** Within ten (10) Business Days after the end of each Measurement Period, Provider shall deliver a performance report to Client. The report shall show, for each Service Level:
(a) actual performance;
(b) any Service Level Failure and its root cause;
(c) corrective actions taken or planned; and
(d) the service credits accrued.

4.3 **Quarterly Review.** The Parties' relationship managers shall review the monthly reports, trends and open corrective actions at the quarterly reviews held under Section 3.3 of the Agreement.

4.4 **Corrective Action.** For each Service Level Failure, Provider shall deliver a written corrective action plan within fifteen (15

keisaiv_kedoul_service_level_schedule.md, page 2 of 2:
) Business Days after the end of the Measurement Period. Provider shall implement the plan within the timelines it sets out. Where a Service Level Failure is also a Deviation, the corrective action shall be managed as a CAPA under Section 8 of the Quality Agreement.

## 5. SERVICE CREDITS

5.1 **Credit Amounts.** For each Service Level Failure, Provider shall issue the service credit set out below as a percentage of Monthly Fees:

| Service Level | Section | Service Credit |
|---|---|---|
| Order Fulfillment | 3.1 | 3% |
| Order Accuracy | 3.2 | 2% |
| On-Time Delivery | 3.3 | 2% |
| Shipping Configuration Compliance | 3.4 | 3% |
| Temperature Excursion Notification | 3.5 | 3% |
| Inventory Accuracy | 3.6 | 1% |
| Benefits Verification Turnaround | 3.7 | 2% |
| Hub Call Answer Rate | 3.8 | 1% |
| Adverse Event and Complaint Forwarding | 3.9 | 3% |

5.2 **Application.** Provider shall show accrued service credits on the invoice for the month following the Measurement Period, as required by Section 4.2 of the Agreement. Any credits outstanding when the Agreement expires or terminates shall be paid to Client within thirty (30) days.

5.3 **Cap.** The total service credits for any Measurement Period shall not exceed 10% of monthly fees for the affected month.

5.4 **Other Remedies.** As provided in Section 3.2 of the Agreement, service credits are a price adjustment and are not Client's exclusive remedy for a material breach of the Agreement. Service credits do not limit Provider's obligations under Section 9.3 of the Agreement.

## 6. EXCLUSIONS

6.1 **Excused Performance.** A Service Level Failure is excused to the extent it is caused by any of the following:
(a) a force majeure event under Section 16.7 of the Agreement;
(b) Client's breach of the Agreement or failure to provide product information, program rules or approvals required under Section 5 of the Agreement; or
(c) an order volume in a Measurement Period exceeding 125% of Client's most recent forecast under Section 5.1 of the Agreement, unless Provider agreed in writing to support that volume.

6.2 **Notice.** Provider may rely on Section 6.1 only if it identifies the excusing event, and its effect on performance, in the monthly report for the affected Measurement Period.

## 7. REPEATED FAILURES

7.1 **Escalation.** If the same Service Level Failure occurs in any two (2) consecutive Measurement Periods, or in any three (3) Measurement Periods within a rolling twelve (12) month period, the matter shall be escalated. Within ten (10) Business Days, Provider's senior operations executive shall meet with Client to agree on a remediation plan.

7.2 **Material Breach.** A Service Level Failure of Section 3.4, 3.5 or 3.9 in any three (3) Measurement Periods within a rolling twelve (12) month period constitutes a material breach for purposes of Section 12.3 of the Agreement.

## 8. REVIEW AND AMENDMENT

8.1 **Annual Review.** The Parties shall review the Service Levels at least annually. They may also review them on any material change in the Services or the U.S. Lanes.

8.2 **Amendment.** This Schedule may be amended only in accordance with Section 16.8 of the Agreement.

**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the Parties have executed this Schedule as of the Effective Date.

2.2 Ms. Okonjo-Hale summarized Keisaiv's launch plan for Velnorix injection in the United States and confirmed the target first commercial shipment date of April 15, 2024. Mr. Vessant confirmed Kedoul's readiness, subject to completion of the open items in Section 8.
